citation: Song, Cotilla-Sanchez, Ghanavati and Hines (2015). Dynamic modeling of cascading failure in power systems. IEEE Transactions on Power Systems 31(3), 2085–2095.
description: COSMIC is a dynamic cascading-outage simulator developed by researchers at Oregon State University and the University of Vermont. It models how power-system failures evolve through coupled electrical dynamics, with supplied MATLAB examples for 9-bus and 39-bus systems. Inputs are a configured power network, component behaviour and disturbances; outputs describe the resulting dynamic outage sequence and system response. The examples are test networks, without a fixed geographic or historical coverage, and simulation timing follows the case configuration. Source is free under GPL-3.0. A limitation is that execution requires separately licensed MATLAB, Simulink and Optimization Toolbox; the README reports testing on MATLAB R2023b on Apple Silicon, not general platform compatibility. COSMIC can support infrastructure cascading-failure and resilience studies. ANDES (model-andes) is related power-system dynamics software. The repository identifies a describing publication and example entry points. No model files or executable software were downloaded.
